name: STACK Infrastructure POR03, Hillsboro
heading: 3. STACK Infrastructure POR03, Hillsboro — Approximately 200 MW Total Critical Capacity
brief: STACK Infrastructure operates and markets its POR03 campus in Hillsboro as a six-building development on approximately 55 acres with 200 MW of total critical capacity . Crucially, STACK separately identifies about 72 MW of operational critical capacity , 25 MW of near-term availability and 96 MW of expansion capacity . Those descriptions distinguish already operating data halls from space that still depends on construction, fit-out and customer requirements. STACK’s rounded campus headline is no

name: Rowan Percheron, Boardman
heading: 2. Rowan Percheron, Boardman — 300 MW Planned Campus
brief: Rowan Digital Infrastructure describes Percheron as a 300 MW hyperscale campus across about 275 acres in the Columbia River Gorge near Boardman. Rowan began site due diligence in late 2022, secured rezoning approvals in 2023, and closed its land acquisition in 2024. The developer lists a phased buildout targeting completion by 2030 . That is a future delivery target, not evidence of 300 MW of energized servers in October 2026.

name: Amazon Threemile/Boardman
heading: 1. Amazon Threemile/Boardman — Hypothetical 1,000 MW Campus Envelope
brief: Amazon Web Services acquired roughly 1,300 acres near Boardman in Morrow County for a potential data center development that has drawn attention under the Threemile or exascale label. Earlier planning documents presented a hypothetical 1,000 MW complex with up to 20 buildings and approximately 4 million square feet . The figure gives a sense of the maximum footprint explored in site planning. It is not a confirmed Amazon construction order, an energized grid connection or the official capacity o

name: Aligned Project Phoenix, Shippingport
heading: 3. Aligned Project Phoenix, Shippingport — 2 GW Planned Campus, Construction Started
brief: Aligned Data Centers broke ground on Project Phoenix on September 10, 2026 , at a former industrial power property near the decommissioned Bruce Mansfield coal plant in Shippingport, Beaver County . The company describes a 2 GW, three-facility campus on a site along the Ohio River, with approximately 2 million square feet of planned data center space . The groundbreaking marks a construction milestone, not the commissioning of 2 GW of servers.

name: TECfusions Keystone Connect, Upper Burrell
heading: 2. TECfusions Keystone Connect, Upper Burrell — 3 GW IT Ambition, Small Initial Phase Operating
brief: TECfusions Keystone Connect , built around the former Alcoa research complex in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County , has the largest explicit IT-power development target among the three entries. The company markets approximately 1,395 to 1,400 acres for an eventual 3 GW of IT load , using former research buildings as the foundation for a much larger AI computing campus. Its Keystone Connect project sheet describes 3 GW as the site’s total capability, not capacity already operating.

name: Homer City Energy Campus, Indiana County
heading: 1. Homer City Energy Campus, Indiana County — 4.4–4.5 GW Planned Power Generation
brief: The largest overall electrical development tied to a Pennsylvania data center campus is Homer City Energy Campus , a more than 3,200-acre redevelopment of the former Homer City coal-fired generating station. Developer Homer City Redevelopment and construction contractor Kiewit plan a large new natural-gas power system, with seven GE Vernova gas turbines intended to supply future AI and high-performance computing facilities as well as the wider grid.

name: Lumen Providence
heading: 3. Lumen Providence — 0.6 MW Listed, Operating
brief: Lumen’s Providence facility is part of the traditional carrier and network-colocation market that developed around downtown Providence. Data Center Map places its Providence 1 site at 375 Promenade Street . Research directories list it as operating and associate roughly 10,400 square feet of total building area with the site. The facility helps regional businesses connect computing equipment to telecom infrastructure rather than functioning as a hyperscale AI training campus.

name: Crown Castle Providence, 300 Carpenter Street
heading: 2. Crown Castle Providence, 300 Carpenter Street — Approximately 1 MW Reported
brief: The operating colocation and network facility at 300 Carpenter Street is associated with former owner Crown Castle Fiber , whose fiber business was sold to a Zayo buyer in 2026. The facility’s source-linked project record identifies it as an active Providence site and notes the ownership transition, but does not confirm a new site-specific operating contract or publish a current electrical rating.

name: Prov.net PVD2, 304 Carpenter Street
heading: 1. Prov.net PVD2, 304 Carpenter Street — 1 MW Critical Power
brief: The best-documented operating capacity among the three belongs to Prov.net’s PVD2 facility at 304 Carpenter Street . In an October 18, 2021 announcement , global network provider Hurricane Electric described the facility as offering up to 15,000 square feet, 1 MW of critical power and 200 tons of N+1 cooling . The power rating describes designed critical-service capacity, not verified continuous consumption . Its site address and network presence remain listed by Hurricane Electric’s own point-o

name: QTS York County
heading: 3. QTS York County — About 300 MW Reported, Under Construction
brief: In the Rock Hill area, QTS is developing a nine-building campus in three phases. The company says its approved project represents approximately $8 billion in planned investment . Four buildings make up its initial phase, while the other five would follow as development proceeds. QTS says two buildings are under construction and none is yet operating; more work is expected as the first phase advances.

name: NorthMark Valara, Spartanburg
heading: 2. NorthMark Valara, Spartanburg — 457 MW Planned, Construction Underway
brief: The Valara High Performance Compute Center is being built at the former Kohler manufacturing site on South Pine Street in Spartanburg. A development agreement considered by Spartanburg County describes a 457 MW data center project over approximately 294 acres, with at least $2.76 billion in proposed investment. Its model centers on substantial on-site power generation rather than treating the entire demand as a simple purchase from an existing local substation.

name: Savannah River Site AI Campus
heading: 1. Savannah River Site AI Campus — 1,000 MW Proposed, Lease Not Final
brief: The largest announced data center project on this list is an approximately 1 GW AI campus at the federal Savannah River Site . On July 20, the Department of Energy’s National Nuclear Security Administration selected Amentum for negotiations over a phased lease. DC BLOX has identified itself as the consortium’s digital-infrastructure partner.

name: Leola Data Center
heading: 3. Leola Data Center — 50 MW Proposed, Local Permit Pending
brief: A proposed 50 MW data center near Leola in McPherson County would occupy a site west of the town near 116th Street and 358th Avenue. Dakota News Now reported that county planners deferred a conditional-use permit decision in August after residents questioned the facility’s water needs and its implications for nearby farms and livestock. The project is proposed—not an operating installation.

name: Big Watt Digital, Sully County
heading: 2. Big Watt Digital, Sully County — 300 MW Expansion Target; About 30 MW Operating
brief: Near Onida, approximately 23 miles north of Pierre, Big Watt Digital operates a roughly 30 MW Bitcoin mining facility . It is the state’s largest operating data center identified by the Legislative Research Council , even though its active size is far below the much larger proposals appearing elsewhere. Bitcoin mining equipment performs repeated SHA-256 hashing rather than general-purpose AI training, but both activities need substantial electrical infrastructure and cooling.

name: Gemini Data Center, Sioux Falls
heading: 1. Gemini Data Center, Sioux Falls — Up to 500 MW Proposed
brief: The largest publicly reported active proposal is Gemini Data Center SD LLC’s 500 MW development on approximately 164 acres near East Rice Street and Veterans Parkway in northeast Sioux Falls. The city’s December 2025 planning materials describe the subdivision request and property size. The city council subsequently approved the necessary zoning and preliminary plans, but those decisions are not an operating permit or evidence of construction completion.

name: xAI Colossus 1, Memphis
heading: 3. xAI Colossus 1, Memphis — 280 MW Reported; Operating
brief: The original Colossus complex occupies the former Electrolux appliance manufacturing plant on Paul R. Lowry Road in southwest Memphis. It became operational in 2024, after the company rapidly installed an enormous cluster of Nvidia GPUs. The Tennessee fiscal note reported 280 MW of capacity for the original Memphis data center, but that does not mean the utility was supplying 280 MW continuously.

name: Meta Gallatin
heading: 2. Meta Gallatin — 300 MW Reported; Operating
brief: Meta’s Gallatin Data Center began serving internet traffic on November 14, 2024 , after breaking ground in 2020. The 300 MW site capacity cited in Tennessee’s fiscal review places it slightly above the original Colossus facility on that published baseline. The figure is not a disclosure that 300 MW of GPUs or servers are currently in use.

name: xAI Colossus 2, Memphis
heading: 1. xAI Colossus 2, Memphis — 1,563 MW Planned in State Report; Partially Operational
brief: The second Colossus development, near Tulane Road and Whitehaven in Memphis, dwarfs the other two sites on Tennessee’s reported planning figures. The state’s February fiscal note assigned it 1,563 MW of planned capacity and anticipated a 2026 start. Subsequent reporting and independent assessments indicate that parts of the campus are now operating, with more infrastructure still being built. The 1,563 MW figure is a planned site rating , not a confirmed current grid draw.

name: Stargate Abilene
heading: 7. Stargate Abilene — 1.2 GW Planned Campus; Partly Operating
brief: The flagship Stargate development at Abilene is one of the state’s clearest examples of the difference between a planned megaproject and equipment already running. Crusoe is developing the campus on Lancium-associated land, with Oracle supplying cloud infrastructure for OpenAI. The larger campus design has been described at 1.2 GW spread across eight buildings, but the full power allocation has not been proven online.

name: Vantage Frontier, Shackelford County
heading: 6. Vantage Frontier, Shackelford County — 1.4 GW Critical IT Planned
brief: Vantage Data Centers’ Frontier development occupies about 1,200 acres in Shackelford County, west of Fort Worth. Vantage’s published specification calls for 1.4 GW of critical IT capacity across ten single-story data centers totaling approximately 3.7 million square feet . That IT figure is different from a gross electrical connection or a generation plant rating.

name: Galaxy Helios, Dickens County
heading: 5. Galaxy Helios, Dickens County — 1.63 GW Approved Campus; 133 MW IT Delivered
brief: The Galaxy Helios complex near Afton began as Bitcoin mining infrastructure and is being redeveloped for AI computing under long-term agreements with CoreWeave. Galaxy reported on July 6 that it had delivered 200 MW gross electrical capacity in its first phase, including 133 MW of critical IT load . This operating milestone is more concrete than a future campus aspiration.

name: Microsoft Pecos, Reeves County
heading: 4. Microsoft Pecos, Reeves County — 2 GW Announced Data Center; Dedicated Power Contract
brief: Microsoft announced on June 22 a new 2 GW data center campus in Pecos , one of its largest planned additions to global capacity. The company describes the investment as multibillion-dollar and expected to take five to seven years, supporting more than 6,000 construction jobs at peak and hundreds of lasting operational positions. The campus is announced, not yet a 2 GW operating installation.

name: IREN Sweetwater Hub
heading: 3. IREN Sweetwater Hub — 2 GW Development Plan; Substation Energized
brief: IREN’s Sweetwater development combines two sites: Sweetwater 1 at 1,400 MW and Sweetwater 2 at 600 MW , for a total announced 2 GW of gross development capacity . Its move from Bitcoin mining toward AI cloud computing has made large land positions, fiber routes, transformers and liquid cooling as important as the mining machines that once defined its business.

name: Tract Caldwell Valley, Caldwell County
heading: 2. Tract Caldwell Valley, Caldwell County — 4 GW Master Plan; Site Development
brief: Tract’s Caldwell Valley Technology Park , north of Lockhart between Austin and San Antonio, encompasses approximately 2,973 acres of land owned and controlled for data center development. Tract says the master plan supports up to about 4 GW of eventual capacity, aided by nearby high-voltage transmission, natural-gas and fiber infrastructure. A land-development capacity rating is not the same thing as fully leased, built or energized data halls.

name: Fermi Project Matador, Carson County
heading: 1. Fermi Project Matador, Carson County — Up to 11 GW Power Campus; 222 MW Initial Tenant Lease
brief: Fermi America’s Project Matador near Amarillo is the highest-capacity development in this ranking, with a claimed 11 GW private HyperGrid energy-campus ambition . The campus is intended to host large-scale AI data centers alongside on-site generating infrastructure. That 11 GW is not a disclosed operating critical IT load ; most of the planned electricity and computing facilities remain to be delivered.

name: Joule High-Performance Compute Campus, Millard County
heading: 3. Joule High-Performance Compute Campus, Millard County — 4 GW Power Plan
brief: Joule Capital Partners is pursuing an AI and high-performance computing campus near Holden in Millard County. On August 7, 2025, Caterpillar and Wheeler Machinery announced an agreement to support as much as 4 GW of electrical energy for Joule’s development. The design uses Caterpillar G3520K gas generator sets and combined cooling, heat and power technology to serve dense computing systems without relying on a conventional utility connection for its main supply.

name: Stratos Project, Box Elder County
heading: 2. Stratos Project, Box Elder County — 7.5–9 GW Proposed Generation; Permits Pending
brief: The Stratos Project in the Hansel Valley is associated with investor Kevin O’Leary and O’Leary Digital. In April, Utah’s Military Installation Development Authority approved creation of a project area, followed by Box Elder County’s May 4 agreement. Early presentations described an ambitious 9 GW long-term power-and-data-center development . More detailed fall 2026 engineering and water filings described about 7.5 GW of long-term gas generation , with a first phase of roughly 1.5–2 GW . The figu

name: Creekstone Delta Gigasite, Millard County
heading: 1. Creekstone Delta Gigasite, Millard County — More Than 10 GW Planned Energy; Work Underway
brief: Near Delta, Creekstone Energy’s Delta Gigasite is the state’s largest disclosed integrated energy-and-data-center vision on this ranking. The company says it owns 1,143 acres , has heavy-industrial zoning and a conditional-use permit, and is developing a greater-than-10 GW behind-the-meter power stack combining gas, solar and other supply.
